data.text: Crowds in Manila for the INC rally so far seem light, but it is a multi-day event, so crowd size is likely to increase before it's over. There is concern an effort to destabilize or overthrow the government of the Philippines may occur during the rallies. The organizers are allied with the Duterte clan and its membership is very loyal to the "church." They wield a lot of influence in the country politically. While this is not the first time rumors like this have been associated with prior similar events, the national mood in the Philippines has never before been so low in terms of dissatisfaction with the political system. The country has been rocked by evidence of historic amounts of corruption, which so far, have not yielded any high profile arrests. I believe, but have no evidence to back up my presumption, that this time those threats are a bit more credible. I believe the Marcos administration is also taking them more seriously as well. The same players tend to always be involved in these things- allegedly disgruntled retired general officers- but I have always suspected that what we hear about disgruntled retired officers is mostly bluster. The seriousness of the current corruption allegations make it possible that they're no longer just bluster. Using the rallies as a basis to incite broad civil unrest or disturbances that could serve as a distraction while a coup attempt is carried out appears to be the major security concern for the Presidential Security Group, the AFP and PNP.

data.text: The Armed Force of the Philippines joins the Philippine National Police and other law enforcement agencies going to alert in Manila and in the National Capitol Region in hopes of deterring civil unrest arising out of an large rally by the religious cult, INC, which is allied with the Duterte clan and factions in the Philippines. There are apparently credible threats of a plot to destabilize or overthrow the Marcos government. I would estimate the response by government security forces to this rally is noticeably larger than past rallies, by perhaps 25-30%

The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Sunday said it is on alert for any sudden incidents which may occur during the series of anti-corruption protests conducted by different groups.

“Kailangan alerto pa rin tayo. Hindi naman puwedeng tanggalin sa equation na maaaring may ibang agenda na puwedeng gamitin itong mga pagkakataong ito para isingit ang kanilang interes,” AFP spokesperson Colonel Francel Padilla said in an interview on Super Radyo dzBB.
